title: Confirmation Rate
scenario: Calculate the confirmation rate for each user. The confirmation rate is the number of 'confirmed' actions divided by the total number of confirmation requests. Users with no requests should have a rate of 0.00. Return the result table as 'user_id' and 'confirmation_rate'.
tableSchema: signups (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME), confirmations (user_id INT, time_stamp DATETIME, action VARCHAR)
hint: Use a LEFT JOIN between Signups and Confirmations. Use IFNULL and AVG(action = 'confirmed') to calculate the rate.
correctQuery: SELECT s.user_id, ROUND(IFNULL(AVG(c.action = 'confirmed'), 0), 2) AS confirmation_rate FROM signups s LEFT JOIN confirmations c ON s.user_id = c.user_id GROUP BY s.user_id;
